history.dynasty: Originated in the 3rd century BCE/Vikram era legends; current structure built in the 11th century CE by the Solanki dynasty; renovated in the 15th century
history.period: Traditional founding by Acharya Sthulabhadra; present shikhara 11th c. CE; idols reinstalled V.S. 1429 (1373/1449 CE accounts vary); Nakoda Bhairav installed V.S. 1511 (1455 CE) by Acharya Kirtiratna Suri
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE -- keep-or-drop decision needed: Shri Nakoda Parshwanath Jain Tirth is one of western Rajasthan's great Jain pilgrimages (administered by the Tapa Gaccha of the Shvetambara Murtipujaka order), dedicated to Lord Parshvanath. Its ancient name was Virampur/Nakornagar; legend says Virsen and Nakorsen built it and Acharya Sthulabhadra consecrated the idols. Damaged in 12th-13th-century invasions (one account says the idols were hidden in Kalidrah village during Alamshsh's invasion, V.S. 1280), it was rebuilt in the 15th century; the mulnayak idol was reinstalled in V.S. 1429 (one account says 1449 CE) and the miraculous guardian deity Nakoda Bhairav in V.S. 1511. It also houses a newly built Samosaran temple with a 90-ft dome. CSV town 'Barmer' must be corrected: the tirth is at Nakoda village in Pachpadra/Balotra tehsil, about 10-13 km from Balotra (NOT Barmer city; ~120 km from Jodhpur). District: Barmer (Nakoda lies in the former Pachpadra tehsil, now in Balotra district since 2023 -- flagged).

name: Jain Temple, Nakoda
town_description: Nakoda is a pilgrim village in the Pachpadra/Balotra tehsil near Balotra town in western Rajasthan, about 13 km from Balotra; besides the temples the tirth has dharamshalas, a bhojanalaya and a goshala.
